title: Custom Keyword Template
description: Use a custom keyword as a template to run complex test logic with multiple data sets.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Templates aren't limited to built-in keywords. You can template YOUR custom keywords too. Create a 'Check System' keyword, then run it for 5 different systems."
story.context: Custom keyword templates let you execute multi-step test logic repeatedly with different inputs. This is more powerful than single keyword templates.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! Your custom keyword ran 5 times—once per system. Each execution logged the system name and status. That's reusable, data-driven testing."

hints: Keyword takes 2 arguments: system name and expected status
Template calls your custom keyword, not built-in
Data rows provide arguments: system name, then status
Order matters: Keywords section before Test Cases section

theory.title: Exercise 2.3.2: Custom Keyword Templates
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Built-in keyword templates are useful, but the real power comes when you template YOUR OWN keywords. Multi-step test logic, executed many times with different data."

Templating Custom Keywords

Any keyword can be templated—including your custom keywords:

*** Keywords ***
Validate Component
    [Arguments]    ${name}    ${min_value}    ${max_value}
    Log    Validating ${name}
    Should Be Greater Than    ${min_value}    0
    Should Be Less Than    ${max_value}    100
    Log    ${name} within range

*** Test Cases ***
Component Validation
    [Template]    Validate Component
    Temperature    20    80
    Pressure       10    90
    Flow Rate      5     95

Benefits:

  • Complex logic (multiple keywords) executed repeatedly
  • Arguments passed to custom keyword
  • Clean data separation from logic
  • Reusable test procedures

Example: Login Validation

*** Keywords ***
Attempt Login
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}    ${should_succeed}
    Log    Trying: ${username} / ${password}
    IF    '${should_succeed}' == 'True'
        Should Not Be Equal    ${password}    wrong
        Log    Login succeeded
    ELSE
        Should Be Equal    ${password}    wrong
        Log    Login failed as expected
    END

*** Test Cases ***
Login Tests
    [Template]    Attempt Login
    admin      password123    True
    user1      wrong          False
    guest      guestpass      True

Three login attempts, different usernames/passwords, validation logic runs each time.

⚠️ Custom Keyword Template Tips

  • Keyword must accept arguments matching data row columns
  • Data row argument count must match [Arguments] count
  • Keyword can contain any complexity (IF, FOR, TRY, etc.)
  • Each data row = one full keyword execution
  • Great for: repeated workflows, batch validations, test scenarios
